summary: Steel Aermotor tower near Tyrone, Huntingdon County: built 1933, opened 1951, removed 1972 or 1977 (sources disagree); no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed. The register gives 1972 and the Forest Lookouts page gives 1977. No source describes what remains.

staffing.status: A towerman used the cabin at the tower base in 1971

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources (owned the tower cabin in 1971)

events.note: The register gives 1933 as the build year.
A July 1933 issue of The Forest Worker reported a plan to move a 60-foot Bald Knob tower to a site near Tyrone and raise it to 80 feet. No source read confirms the move or the height.
Opened October 1, 1951, after radio and telephone equipment was installed the week before (Huntingdon Daily News).
In May 1953 John Cannistraci was in charge of the Bald Eagle fire tower and reported most fires to local crews (Tyrone Daily Herald).
Two teenage boys admitted vandalizing the Tyrone tower cabin, per a November 16, 1955 report.

Vandals caused several hundred dollars of damage to the fire tower and cabin on Bald Eagle mountain, north of Tyrone (October 26, 1956 report). The sources do not say outright that this is the same lookout.
The log cabin at the tower base was used by the towerman; it was burglarized in April 1971.
The register gives 1972; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1977.
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg.

corrections.why: 18.3 m is 60 feet, the height of the Bald Knob tower before the planned move. The July 1933 report planned 80 feet after the move, and no source read confirms the Tyrone tower's height.
The current value is a fragment of a newspaper date. The only agency these sources name for the Tyrone site is the Department of Environmental Resources, which owned the tower cabin in 1971.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says 1972 and the Forest Lookouts page says 1977. The story reports both dates and does not choose one.
Sources call the tower both Tyrone and Bald Eagle. The 1956 report places a fire tower on Bald Eagle mountain north of Tyrone. Treated as one lookout; this is an inference, not a stated fact.

notes_for_editor: The Huntingdon Daily News article behind the 1951 opening could not be read (HTTP 429 on two tries), so that date rests on the Forest Lookouts quotes. The 1933 move of a 60-foot Bald Knob tower is a plan, not a confirmed event. Two web searches turned up nothing on the Tyrone site itself. Brief agency value 'July 1933:' looks like a parsing error. Brief coordinates 40.6846, -78.2123 were not checked against any source. Worth a later search for the site's current status and the 1951 article.
